Maud MendWell’s
Mystery Mischief

Thrice Thimble Lane has always had three houses. Since Tuesday it has had four.

By Tibby TattleTwill, Town Correspondent, The Daily Yarn

Residents of Frays End woke this week to find, quite suddenly, one lane longer than it was. Thrice Thimble Lane has had three houses for as long as anyone can remember, and is named for them. Now it has four. A crooked cottage sits at the end of the lane, with washing on the line and a wren singing far too loudly for her size.

The cottage belongs, by every account, to Maud MendWell, the solitary KnitWitch whose home turns up where it is needed rather than where it was put. It has once again confounded the post office.

By the time our reporter arrived, a sizeable queue had formed in the lane - torn coats, odd socks, a tired grandfather and a Patchling clutching a frayed blanket. Buttons in hand they waited, Weft the wren, keeper of the washing line, heralding each new arrival.

How to Call on Maud

  1. Knock twice.
  2. Leave a single shiny button of indigo or azure.
  3. Go home. Don’t wait up.
  4. Don’t go looking for the cottage. It will find you.

Threadlings of Frays End in need of mending, take note: last seen on Thrice Thimble Lane. By Friday, it may not be.

Faction Watch

KnitWitches Patrol the Fraying

KnitWitches, most often solitary beings unless drawn to their coven for some mysterious who-knows-what… or when, have been spotted across the Fraying in numbers. Cowled and silent, they are causing quite the stir in the border towns of Threadbare with this unusual behaviour.

Fray Sightings

Citizens, Be Vigilant!

  • InkDrinkers · SunSpun Sands. Splugs seen crossing the dunes east. Two caravans unaccounted for; a third arrived with every ledger blank.
  • MemoryMoths · HemsHollow. Dusters reported by the East Wall. Hum, keep lamps lit, walk in pairs. Residents woke unsure which house was theirs.
  • Storyvores · The Fraying. A Gobbler suspected beneath the road south of LinenVille. Patchlings: no stories aloud on the way to school.

As reported to the Frays End Watch.

Classifieds

  • Wanted: Buttons of indigo or azure, any size, shiny preferred. Top price paid, no questions asked. Enquire at the haberdasher’s, Frays End market.
  • Services: Free lens polishing at the University of the Unseen, Frays End, to any traveller who brings an unsolved mystery.

WonderWing Blooms Bring Life to Old Looms

This year’s Whisper of WonderWings, fresh from their Manuscrysalis, have been found to be particularly drawn to old and broken looms across Threadbare. WonderBlooms are bursting to life as these creatures land on the largely forgotten and disused weaving machines, drawing attention to them and, in some cases, attracting weavers to dust them down and repair them.
